name: Dreams Los Cabos Golf Resort & Spa

kids_club.evidence: Explorer's Club (3-12) is included and listed as open 9am-10pm, with its own fenced playground and private splash pad; recent parents of 4- and 7-year-olds say their kids loved it.

water_play.evidence: Children's pool with a splash pad and a water slide into a lower pool; no full water park.

beach.evidence: Not safe for young children. The Sea of Cortez beach here is posted with red flags all year because of strong undertow and a sharp drop-off just past the break, and water sports are not allowed. The nearest calm swimming is a cove 10-15 minutes' walk away or Medano Beach about 20 minutes' drive. Sargassum is not an issue on this coast.

rooms.evidence: All-suite resort (about 287-308 suites, 650 sq ft and up) with junior suites in king-plus-sofa-bed or two-double configurations and one-bedroom suites; connecting rooms unverified.

food.evidence: Only four à la carte restaurants (Mediterranean, seafood, French, grill) plus a buffet. Recent family reviews say getting kids fed early is a nightly scramble: queues before the 5:30pm opening, and only two venues have kids' menus. The food itself is praised.

transfer.evidence: In Cabo Real on the Tourist Corridor; listed at about 25-30 minutes from SJD.

condition.evidence: Built in 1997 and rebuilt after Hurricane Odile in 2014, with a renovation listed for 2024. Recent reviews are mostly positive, though some mention dated furnishings and renovation dust.

kids_club.name: Explorer's Club
kids_club.notes: Private splash pad, fenced playground, climbing wall and weekly campouts. The children's pool is at the front of the resort, out of sight of the main pool.

pros: Kids' club runs 9am-10pm with its own splash pad
All-suite rooms with space for a family
No sargassum on the Pacific/Sea of Cortez side
cons: Ocean is red-flagged and unsafe for young children: beach time means sand only
Only four à la carte restaurants, with nightly queues for early kids' dinners
No water park, just a kids' pool, splash pad and one slide
Kids' pool is out of sight of the main pool
Getting to a swimmable beach means a walk or a taxi
verdict: A good kids' club and pool setup, but no swimmable sea and a nightly scramble for early dinners make it a weak fit for a beach week with young children.
